items.line: und heißt נער (Chulin 53, a), während des Verzehrens knurrt er (Be-
items.note: Chulin 53a distinguishes שאג from נער (the roar on seeing the prey), so נער is the term cited. Reading B, עוא, is not a Hebrew word.

items.line: Sanhedrin 102, a heißt es: אין ארי דורס ונוהם, wo das Wort דורס
items.note: Two verbs in a row, 'דורס ונוהם', most naturally take the conjunction ו. Lewysohn's remark that דורס should be struck points back to the familiar phrase 'אין ארי נוהם'. Reading B is grammatically possible, so this is not certain.

items.line: gelbe Feuchtigkeit (Arist. l. c. 9, 31, 3), welche ויהורא (Chulin ibid.
items.note: Chulin 53a speaks of the lion's 'zihara' (זיהורא), a yellowish poisonous fluid; ויהורא is not a word.

items.line: טגרים (Τίγρις) und umschrieben: אריא דבי עילאי „Löwe des
items.note: The heading transliterates Greek Τίγρις, so the expected form is טגריס (Talmudic טיגריס). The plural-looking טגרים is a final ם/ס OCR confusion.

items.line: benennt ihn, wie wir gesehen, auch der Talmud neben טגרים auch
items.note: The tiger's name transliterates Greek/Latin tigris, so the final letter is samekh: טגריס (cf. Talmud טיגריס). טגרים would be a plural form that does not fit as the animal's name.
